exposure: chronic diseases associated with bone fragility
cohort: The study included 155 women with Pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis (PLAO) and 182 women without PLAO from an Italian survey.
finding: Pregnancy and lactation-associated osteoporosis (PLAO) is associated with pre-pregnancy factors like BMI <18.5, low calcium intake, older age at pregnancy, previous fragility fractures, and chronic diseases, as well as during-pregnancy factors such as insufficient weight gain, LMWH use, and low calcium intake.
cross-section timing: Data on clinical history, lifestyle, nutritional habits, and pregnancy characteristics were collected retrospectively via a questionnaire from women who had experienced PLAO (cases) and those who had not (controls).
